numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Non-finite float input (inf/-inf) passed through int(item) raises a bare OverflowError that errors="coerce" cannot catch. An overflowing round float or integer with a coarse unit (e.g. Timedelta(1e19, unit="s") or Timedelta(10**19, unit="s")) goes through np.timedelta64(value, unit) and also raises a bare OverflowError.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Non-finite floats should fall through to _numeric_to_td64ns and raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta (a ValueError), or give NaT under errors="coerce". Overflowing round float or integer input with a coarse unit should raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta rather than a bare OverflowError.
trigger_conditions: Passing float('inf') or float('-inf') to Timedelta or to_timedelta
Passing inf/-inf floats in an object array to to_timedelta, including with errors="coerce"
Passing an overflowing round float or integer with a coarse unit such as unit="s", e.g. Timedelta(1e19, unit="s") or Timedelta(10**19, unit="s")

input_output_examples.source: commit:BUG: Timedelta/to_timedelta raise bare OverflowError for inf/overflowing floats (GH#63275)

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: inf and -inf floats; overflowing round float or int such as Timedelta(1e19, unit="s") and Timedelta(10**19, unit="s")
category_specific_evidence: The violated contract is that non-finite floats (inf/-inf) should raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta, a ValueError, rather than a bare OverflowError from int(item), so that errors="coerce" yields NaT.

Expected behavior per the test: Timedelta(np.inf) and Timedelta(-np.inf) raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta matching "without overflow"; to_timedelta(val) raises the same; to_timedelta(val, errors="coerce") is NaT.
Round float overflow: Timedelta(1e19, unit="s") should raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta, not a bare OverflowError from np.timedelta64(value, unit).
Integer overflow: Timedelta(10**19, unit="s") is cited in the PR body as going through np.timedelta64 and raising a bare OverflowError before the fix.

Fix mechanism: item.is_integer() replaces int(item) == item in array_to_timedelta64 and the scalar Timedelta.__new__ float branch, so float('inf').is_integer() is False and the value falls to _numeric_to_td64ns.
Pandas 2.3.x reportedly gave NaT/OutOfBoundsTimedelta for these inputs, per the PR body.
reproduction_risks: NaN never reaches the is_integer branch; it is caught earlier by checknull_with_nat_and_na, so NaN is not a valid reproduction input for this path.
The np.timedelta64 OverflowError wrapping only applies when unit is not 'ns'.
The issue discussion concerns dtype and unit-of-output choices, not this specific exception bug, so those passages do not supply numerical expected values.
The test matches the message substring "without overflow"; a reproduction should not depend on other message text.
